title: In Bengal, Tribunal Remedy has Been Slowest Where the SIR Has Affected Muslim Voters the Most
summary: Highlights that out of the 72,05,162 names found 'not eligible to vote', 18.98 lakh were Muslims based on a RTI response. Malda and Murshidabad districts share 6,83,683 exclusions, out of this 6,52,858 were Muslims. 16 constituencies across the state had no restorations. In Uttar Dinajpur, 90.4% marked not eligible were Muslims. However, it also showed faster decisions at the Tribunal level in comparison to Malda and Murshidabad.

title: TDP goons snatch nomination papers of the woman YSRCP candidate in JD Nellore
summary: The TDP (ruling party) goons snatched nomination papers of a YSRCP female candidate who had gone to file her MPTC nomination for local body elections. The police stood by watching the act.

summary: Goons run and snatch nomination papers from a woman who was walking in a group of three to file for local body elections.

title: TDP members snatched and tore opposition member's nomination form in front of electoral officers
summary: TDP members seen snatching and tearing nomination for local body elections from right before nomination in front of electoral officers.

title: TDP goon snatches nomination papers from returning officer in Andhra Pradesh, Penukonda, Sri Sathya Sai District
summary: A TDP goon snatches nomination papers from the Returning Officers and tears them for local body elections.

title: Nomination papers forcefully snatched and torn inside the nomination centre
summary: A man reached the nomination centre with his papers to nominate himself for the local body elections where he was held by another man and his papers were snatched. This was done in front of the electoral officers at Chitoor JD office.

summary: A voter slip shows the name Mohd. Iqbal Bheek Mangte hain.

title: Election Commission's appeals against 16.10 lakh cleared voters raise legal questions
summary: More than 16 lakh voters who were excluded in SIR in West Bengal were cleared by judicial officers. However, the Election Commission of India filed appeals against the exclusions. However, the officials who filed the appeals might not have the authority to do that as under the Representation of the People Act.Only the CEO/DEO/ERO/AERO are authorized. The Election Commission in its affidavit to the Supreme Court said that the 'officers had the authority to file the appeals as per the order of this Hon'ble (Supreme) Court.'But the affidavit only mentions authorities as per the Representation of People Act.

title: SIR: ECI moves to strike off 76,000 judge-cleared voters in Bengal's border seats, nearly all Muslim names
summary: The Election Commission of India appealed against the judicial officers' decision in two constituencies in West Bengal, Murshidabad and Malda which had cleared 76,000 voters. Mostly all the names excluded are commonly associated with the Muslim community (99.9% in Samserganj and 99.6% in Sujapur). If these appeals are upheld, the constituencies could see a reduction in the number of voters cleared by the judicial officers. Further, in Samserganj, the officers deleted 69% (1,08,400) voters under adjudication leaving only 33,152 on the rolls. ECI appealed against 15,195 of these exclusions. In Sujapur, of the 1,34,521 voters under adjudication judgers deleted only 20% and cleared the rest 1,07,690. ECI challeneged the inclusion of 56.7% (61,066) of them. This means Samserganj would lose a total of 83% voters placed under adjudication and Sujapur would lose 65%. Samserganj has approximately 72% Muslim population while Sujapur has 75%.

title: In Delhi, BJP booth agents file deletion forms against Muslim voters living at their addresses
summary: Mustafabad constituency in Delhi saw the highest number of Form 7 applications with 843 objections (since August 31). Further, of the 597 objection forms filed by third parties, 96% named BJP's booth level agents (BLA) as 'objectors'. Further, 572 Form 7s are filed against Muslims electors across the constituency. It excludes people living in the area for over two decades. A total of 28 voters were sought to be deleted from the area citing 'absent/ permanently shift' or 'death' as the reason.' All of the electors were found to be living in the area at their addresses. Further, 10 BLAs filed more than 30 Form 7 and 9s over 25 applications. However, ECI's directive of October 9 only permits a cap of 10 forms per individual elector. BLAs can submit up to 10 forms a day including Forms 6, 7 and 8 which are filled by individual electors. They are also required to submit a list of applications with an undertaking that they verified the details. The BLAs also gave no undertaking about the objections the filed. The people against whom the objections were filed said they do not know who the person is (objector has to be a registered elector in the constituency). One of the objectors initially said he resides in the area, then said he did not file the objections and is not a BLA or associated with any political party.

title: Over 340 voter ID cards found on Narmada riverbank in MP's Khargone, Congress seeks FIR
summary: 343 voter ID cards with addresses of Indore were found at the Narmada riverbank in Khargone district in Madhya Pradesh. The cards belong to the Rau constituency and the addresses listed on Electoral Photo ID Cards (EPICs) include Tilak Nagar and Aastha Palace. It was alleged that the card carried 2016 as the year however, the digital card format was introduced in 2021. Similar discoveries were also made in Chhatarpur, another district in Madhya Pradesh where hundreds of voter ID cards were found in October 2025 in the Raja Talab.

title: Testimony of a single mother excluded in the SIR Process
summary: It is unclear where the woman if from. She is a single mother who was excluded in the SIR process. She shared her experience during the public impeachment of Gyanesh Kumar. She got to know that her vote was deleted and how she used it as an identity card for scholarships and opening bank account. She is an Indian citizen and she says she has to work and this way, the government is creating ways for her to just stand in long queues. If she has to stand in another queue, how will she get her daughter educated and how will she plan her future.

title: Delhi SIR: INDIA bloc demands exercise rollback, alleges large-scale voter exclusion without verification
summary: The INDIA bloc alliance demanded that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls should be scrapped. They alleged that the voters were wrongly excluded and that there were errors in the voter records. It was also alleged that the exercise has disproportionately impacted poor workers, tenants, and the residents of unauthorized settlements. It was further alleged by CPI(M) that the survey across Assembly constituencies had found instances of voters being marked 'permanently shifted' without the officials meeting them in person. In E-2 Block, Sonia Vihar in Karawal Nagar, 40% of the entries examined by CPI (M) were incorrect. They filed a complaint with the Electoral Registration Officer and the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer. Maya, a woman from Burari shared that 7-8 family members did not figure on the draft roll even though they were born, brought up, and married in Delhi. Further, it was also alleged by CPI (M) that tenants who had moved to close addresses within the same constituency were denied enumeration forms and marked as shifted. Residents of the areas where demolitions were carried out such as Madrasi camp, Navjeevan camp, and Wazirpur were also affected. Of the total 1.45 lakh voters in Delhi before revision, 97.5 lakh names figured in the draft rolls. 47.5 lakh were marked as absent, shifted, deador duplicate (ASDD) and were thus excluded from the draft lists. INDIA bloc alleged that 11 lakh names had been removed even before the SIR process began. They also highlighted inconsistencies from Pilibhit in UP, where discrepancies were found in 10,470 of the 13,779 approved Form 8 applications for voter-detail corrections.

title: '13,150 Names Altered': UP CEO Orders Action Against Officials After Opposition Flags Glitches in Pilibhit Voter List
summary: The Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) in UP directed legal action against two electoral officers in Pilibhit and removed them from voter list duties. The discrepancies were related to searching Electors Photo Identity Card (EPIC) numbers of certain voters online which displayed details of other individuals. Samajwadi Party (SP) had claimed previously that they had found many duplicate voters in the voter roll. The District Election Officers (DEO) were asked to thoroughly review the voter lists across the assembly constituencies. This comes after Congress alleged that they found major irregularities around more than 16,000 voter entries in the voter list of the Pilibhit Sadar assembly alone. They found that even after the final draft of the electoral roll for UP was released names associated with 13,510 voters were subsequently altered between July and September, even though their EPIC numbers and serial numbers remained unchanged. For example, at booth number 409, voter serial no. 220 was registered as Ashik Ali; however, on searching his EPIC no., it displayed the details of Khalil Khan.

title: Mahua Moitra's X post with a man excluded in the SIR process
summary: Man named Kunne Lal declared dead in the SIR process. As per Mahua Moitra's post, he was declared dead by the BLO without visiting his house for inquiry. He lives in a Basti in New Delhi.

title: Who exposed irregularities involving 13,150 voters?: Congress worker got first clue from cyber cafe; had to examine 348,000 records
summary: Congress claimed that 13,150 voters' names were changed in Pilibhit Sadar constituency. The names were correct in the final electoral roll published on 10 April 2026 and were altered between July and 15 October. Other details like EPIC numbers, age, gender was correct but their own name and father's name changed. As per Congress, all the affected voters were Muslims. A team of 55 people checked the EPIC numbers of around 3.48 lakh voters listed around all 419 polling booths in the Assembly constituency. This started when a man went to a cyber cafe to print his voter ID. He gave his EPIC ID multiple times, but his name and father's name came out wrong on the card. A lawyer present there worked with the cyber cafe owner and discrepancies for around 60 people came up in one night. The lawyer Rehan and the cyber cafe owner Gangwar and team checked 3,48,937 EPIC numbers of voters registered across 419 polling booths. They uncovered three types of discrepancies involving 16,554 votes. The biggest case involved 13,150 voters whose names and fathers' names appeared differently despite their EPIC numbers and serial numbers staying the same. Second and third categories involved removal of 804 voters' names from the list and the addition of around 2,600 new names. However, the process of submitting Forms 6, 7, and 8 had closed on 10 April itself. In addition to this, in some cases the mobile numbers linked to EPIC numbers were also changed. 804 people whose names were deleted allegedly belonged to one community and did not vote for BJP and the 2,600 added were BJP supporters. Further, they checked 500 of the 2,600 new names added and could not find the concerned people in the villages listed in the records.

title: 'Husband Husband' to '????' and 'XXX': After SIR, Bengaluru's electoral rolls riddled with errors
summary: The final electoral rolls published in Bangalore carried multiple errors, like 'XXX' or '??????K' in place of names or missing relatives' names and constaining single letters, email IDs. Inconsistencies in at least 1,000 entries alone were found. In some cases, voters listed one after the other as per serial numbers had their names and relatives' names replaced by jumble letters which made it impossible for them to identify them from the entries. In the Dasarahalli constituency, part no. 324 which has 425 electors, a large number of consecutive entries carried garbled names. The electors' and relatives' names at serial numbers 4 to 7, 143 to 152, 152 to 157, 300 to 302, 306 to 313, 327 to 330, and 336 to 340 appeared as stringes of unfamiliar characters. For example, serial number 327 listed the elector's name as 'µ¢µÌèÌ' and relative's name as 'ÏÇµÈèÈ'. The errors in the names of relatives' names included issues like column left blank or containing only a single letter in several entries. Others were also listed as 'NA', 'None' or had the relationship listed in place of their names like 'Husband', 'Wife', or 'Mother'. In Dasarahalli, for an elector named Kavitha, her name was split between English and Kannada even in the English version of the roll. For relative's name, it read 'Husband Husband'. In Chamarajpet, Abdul Salam had 'Wife' written in relative's name and in Mahadevapura, some entries had only a single letter like 'S' or 'B' in relative's name. Some entries had details like email ID or dates mentioned, which had no association to the details. In Yelahanka, polling part 332, an elector's relative's name had 'rakshithagowda1430@gmail.comgowda'. In BBMP South district, the relative's name mentioned was 'Syed Apsar KZW1566785'. Another 50 year old man's name was listed as 'Channapa Gowda Patil 01/06/1974' and another 44 year old woman's name was listed as '??????K'. BLOs said these errors were due to software glitches.

summary: One person, Abhishek K N filed 4 applications (form 6) in a single day after his name was missing from 176 Bangalore South Assembly Constituency. He received four different EPIC/ voter IDs.

title: Booth capturing by NDA in Andhra Pradesh
summary: After reports of tearing and snatching of nomination papers for the local body elections repolling was announced. However, video shows an unauthorized person at the polling centre stamping pages on his own.

title: 'Direct Attack on Democracy': 31 election incidents, 16 nomination paper destruction cases in Andhra
summary: In Andhra Pradesh 31 election related incidents were recorded across 13 districts during the filing of nominations for the Mandal Parishad Territorial Constituency (MPTC) and Zila Parishad Territorial Constituency (ZPTC) elections. The incidents included occurences like clashes, attacks on candidates and destruction of nomination papers. The DGP called the destruction of nomination papers a direct attack on democracy and said there would be criminal actions against those responsible. As per the DGP's office 22 incidents involved violence, clashes or public order disturbances while 9 were separately reported incidents of nomination papers being snatched or torn. Across all, there were 16 incidents of nomination papers being snatched, torn or destroyed. Anantpur had the highest number of incidents (8) followed by Annamayya, Kadapa, Prakasam and Tirupati, with three each. Chittoor, Sri Sathya Sai and Palnadu reported two incidents each, while Nellore, Kurnool, Markapuram, Nandyal and Eluru reported one each. Due to the violence, 4 vehciles were set on fire and two residential houses attacked/ destroyed and one being demolished using an earth-mover. Further 6 incidents involved stone pelting or attacks with stones and sticks. There were several injuries to people and to a police constable. Candidates belonging to TDP, YSRCP, and CPI (M), along with an independent candidate among those targeted. A total of 16 cases (including counter cases) were registered while cases related to 11 further incidents being processed. At least 54 people were named accused and four apprehended at the scene. Police also used lathi charge and fired tear gas shells to disperse the mob attacking a police vehicle. Videos and photographs were being used to identify more people.

title: In Karnataka seat where 'vote chori' claims first surfaced, over 800 voter IDs linked to 397 names after SIR
summary: In Mahadevapura Assembly constituency, 803 voter IDs were linked to 397 people. In many cases, more than 3 voter IDs were issued under one person's name. This is the same constituency where the vote theft allegations emerged in 2024 when Rahul Gandhi alleged alleged that more than one lakh fake or stolen voters had been systematically engineered in the area to manipulate the 2024 Bengaluru Central Lok Sabha election. The seat is represented by BJP as of now. After the SIR, some voters were found listed in two different constituencies with the same Elector's Photo Identity Card (EPIC) numbers. In some other cases, voters were issued multiple EPIC IDs. For a woman named Madhumita, her name appeared in final SIR rolls in both Mahadevapura, Part 180 and Hebbal, Part 62 with the same EPIC number and father's name and age. For Chitra, her name appeared in Mahadevapura Part 90 and Dasarahalli, Part 251 with the same EPIC details. There were at least 7 such cases. Thus, 7 EPIC entries accounted for 14 entries in the final rolls. Three each between Mahadevapura and Dasarahalli and Mahadevapura and Sarvagnanagar, and one between Mahadevapura and Hebbal. There was another set of cases where individuals were issued multiple EPIC IDs. For example, Santosh Kumar aged 63 has five voter IDs, three in same polling station (part 232) and one each in Parts 233 and 234. His daughter Kriti aged 27 also had two voter IDs in Parts 232 and 234. Her details in both tne entries remained identical except that in one it did not mention the house number. Both also had Santosh Kumar as her father. There were further more than 500 cases in Mahadevapura in which the same perrson had two or more voter IDs within a polling station. In other 300 cases, the same person had multuple IDs but across different polling stations in the constituency. In Part 2, two consecutive serial numbers, 497 and 498 are both listed under the name of Nithin aged 18 with Prakash as his father. The only difference being that in one the house number was listed as 00 and the other as 025. A woman named Girija aged 51 years whose name was deleted from draft rolls appeared twice in the final rolls (part 484 and 487). The Form 9 report showed she had applied with Form 6 twice. Both the entries mention the same address at which she had been marked 'permanently shifted.' This led to her deletion from draft rolls.

title: SIR: Of over a crore deletion, 4.48 lakh return; one-third additions are first-time voters
summary: More than 1/3rd (36%) of Form 6 applications accepted for inclusion in Karnataka's final electoral roll during the SIR were filed by oung/ first-time voters aged 18 and 19. This means, only 4.48 lakh of the 1.07 crore people excluded at the draft stage got back on the rolls, because a significant share of the additions comes from the new voters. Between June 16 (date on which rolls were frozen) and September 23 (last day to file claims and objections) the CEO received 7,87,534  Form 6 applications. 76,176 were rejected and 7,08,110 were accepted. Of those accepted, 2,59,838 were filed by voters aged 18 and 19. This also means that 99.32 lakh names remained deleted in the final list. A part of these deletions are the redundancies in the rolls, such as 7.09 lakh duplicate entries and 16.39 lakh deceased voters, and the remaining, and the largest share (above 84.46 lakh) come from absent and shifted residence. However, only 4.48 lakh of those deleted at the draft stage managed to get back on the rolls, as the rest of the new additions are those filed by new electors. The maximum deletions came from Bangalore, where the electorate shrunk from 1.03 crore before the revision to 59.08 lakh in the final rolls. During the claim and objection period, there was a net addition of 2.74 lakh names. Further, of these 41,141 (16.66%) are new voters aged 18 and 19. Hence, more than 43 lakh people disenfranchised during the draft stage continue to be off the final rolls. Kalaburagi, which had the second largest deletions in the state, had more than 23.71 lakh electors before the SIR. At the draft stage, more than 5.21 lakh names were deleted (22%) and left 18,49,585 on the rolls. The final list had 18,94,144 electors, just an addition of 44,559 from the draft stage. Of these, 12, 985 were new voters aged 18 and 19, accounting for 29.12% of the additions. The remaining 31,574 were those seeking to get back on the rolls after being excluded under Absent, Shifted, Dead, and Duplicate category. More than 4.77 lakh names deleted at the draft stage remained excluded.

title: SIR: Over 61,000 marked 'ineligible'; foreign citizen count remains undetermined
summary: The CEO Karnataka said that of the 43.82 lakh notices generated during SIR due to logical discrepancy and no mapping, at least 1,88,324 names were deleted from the final electoral roll with around 61,900 voters declared 'ineligible' following hearings on notices by EROs and AEROs. After the hearings, 43,20,957 names were retained for the final roll and 61,867 marked ineligible (grounds like acquiring foreign citizenship and being unreachable during the notice hearings among others). Further, 1,24,327 Form 7 applications were auto-generated when voters applied for change of residence through Form 8 to update their names from previous addresses. After the publication of draft roll, another 1,091 voters were identified as dead, while 184 names deleted after the voters were marked absent during the notice phase. Even though the main aim of SIR was to identify foreign nationals, there have been no concrete figures on how many foreign citizens were identified during the exercise. The category of 'Others' was merged with 'absent'. Karnataka (unlike other SIRs) had classified ASDDO (Absent, Shifted, Dupicate, Dead, and Others) category simply as 'Others', with 3,83,884 names falling under it. With this, the numbers under 'absent' went up to 19,00,926 from over 15 lakh in the draft roll. (Earlier it was said that Others included people who refused to sign the enumeration forms and absent for those who couldnt be reached during the process or couldnt get the enumeration form).

title: Karnataka SIR: 64.5 lakh voters potentially missing in rolls, majority of them young
summary: Around 64.5 lakh electors were potentially missing from the final electoral rolls of Karnataka after the SIR based on the Elector to Population ratio (it is the ration b/w total number of electors on the rolls and the estimated population in 2026 in all gae groups including those under 18) of 66.11. The age group of 18 to 29 accounted for the majority of missing names (out of 64.5 lakh 38.41 lakh, i.e., 59.5%). However, the esimated population should have been around 6.89 crore out of which 5.19 crore eligible to vote. Hence, that should have been the final number, however, the final rolls had only 4,54,55,689 electors (excluding service electors) which is short of 64.5 lakh voters. Karnataka had 5.54 crore electors before the SIR process had commenced which was above the estimated population for 18+ age group. However, with the SIR process the deletion of redundant entries and duplicated and deceased voters was expected. But out of 1.08 crore deletion of names during the enumeration phase, only  23.5 lakh (21.8%) were deleted as duplicates and deceased and remaining 78.2% as shifted or absent.Only 8.2 lakh net additions were made during the Claims and Objections phase. For the 18 and 19 age group, the estimated population is 20.66 lakh but had only 6.83 lakh electors. Similarly, for 20-29 age group, the estimated population was 1.11 crore but the roles had only 86.56 lakh first-time electors and 24.58 lakh voters seem to be left out. On a genderwise assessment, between age 18 to 29 there was an underenrolment of women, which increased above 30. More men were deleted during the SIR, as the gender ration went up from 1,007 women for every 1,000 men to 1,017 in final SIR. Further, in the age group of 50 and above, the enrolment was close to the estimated populaion. In the groups, women between 60-69 and men between 70 to 79, there were more electors than estimated population. Further, the E to P ratio for 13 constituencies was less than 50 with most of them in and around Bangalore and BTM Layout having the lowest at 39.23. Its electoral rolls also shrank from 2.82 lakh to 1.41 lakh (more than 50%). Economist Jean Dreze pointed out that E to P of 66.11 is way below 75% which is the estimated part of adults in the population of the state.

title: 2.4 crore difference in UP panchayat and rural Assembly voter lists, EX orders two rolls to be matched
summary: The UP CEO asked the district election officers to match Assembly electoral rolls with those of panchayats and urban local bodies after a difference of 2.4 crore voters emerged between the panchayat poll electoral rolls and the rural voter count identified during the preparation of the Assembly electoral rolls. The fresh exercise will happen till 1 January 2027 and will help in identifying the 'eligible citizens' whose names are missing from the Assembly voters' list as a part of the Special Summary Revision- 2027. Further, the number of women voters in the current Assembly electoral rolls was 'abnormally  low.' The number of poling stations has also dropped in UP from 1,77,516 to 1,73,730 following the 'rationalization' approved by the Election Commission. It was carried out on the prescribed norm of 1,200 voters per polling station.
